user_query: Distribute all the unique city pairs into the distance ranges 0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, and 6000+, based on their average distance of all routes between them. Then how many pairs are there in the distance range with the fewest unique city paires?
clean_summary: The original symmetric CASE WHEN on city names grouped routes bidirectionally, but the GOLD logic treats departure→arrival pairs distinctly; removing that CASE WHEN and selecting the cities directly corrected the bin counts and produced the expected minimum of 6.
database_memories: ENSURE: In the city_pair_distances CTE, select dep_city_en AS city1 and arr_city_en AS city2 directly instead of applying a CASE WHEN for symmetric pairing | CONTEXT: city_pair_distances CTE aggregates flight routes using dep_city_en and arr_city_en; using CASE WHEN to reorder these cities merges distinct directional routes | WHEN_TO_CHECK: When defining the SELECT clause and GROUP BY in the city_pair_distances CTE | EXAMPLE_USAGE:
SELECT CASE WHEN dep_city_en < arr_city_en THEN dep_city_en ELSE arr_city_en END AS city1,
CASE WHEN dep_city_en < arr_city_en THEN arr_city_en ELSE dep_city_en END AS city2,

VERIFY: In the city_pair_distances CTE, GROUP BY dep_city_en and arr_city_en to preserve directional pairings | CONTEXT: Grouping on swapped city1/city2 pairs collapses departure→arrival routes into undifferentiated bins; distance bins must reflect true direction | WHEN_TO_CHECK: When writing the GROUP BY clause in the city_pair_distances CTE | EXAMPLE_USAGE:
SELECT dep_city_en AS city1, arr_city_en AS city2, distance_bin, COUNT(*)
SELECT dep_city_en AS city1, arr_city_en AS city2, distance_bin, COUNT(*)
generic_memories: VERIFY: Avoid CASE WHEN transformations that reorder or normalize paired columns when directionality matters | PRINCIPLE: Conditional swapping of two columns merges distinct records into a single group, leading to incorrect aggregation if order is significant | WHEN_TO_APPLY: Whenever grouping or aggregating on paired or directional data fields | EXAMPLE_USAGE:
Situation: columns A (source) and B (target) represent directional pairs.
SELECT CASE WHEN A < B THEN A ELSE B END AS src,
CASE WHEN A < B THEN B ELSE A END AS tgt,
SELECT A AS src, B AS tgt, COUNT(*)
